tasks.objective: Fix the reported inability to explicitly create fourth/1 Islamic Studies after it was deleted. A fresh deliberate create of a currently absent class/subject is allowed; it is not restore/replay of a deleted identity. Existing src/store.js createTeaching selects any matching tuple including deleted and throws; makeTeaching uses a deterministic ID, and apply_sync_v2_teaching_creation_command also rejects tombstoned tuples. Trace actual current Section/Teaching selection and server bindings before changing. Preserve the simplified N13 form, current date controls, N94 offline scoring, N97 Sync status and N98 ordering. Do not just remove the message or resurrect old IDs/data.
acceptance: Whole-class deletion followed by explicit create with same grade/label/subject yields a new Section and Teaching identity and clean default data. Subject-only deletion while other subjects/roster remain permits a new Teaching identity attached to that same live Section. Never un-delete old row, reuse retired identity, erase tombstones/receipts, or bring back old grades/attendance/history.

Active duplicate same owner/section/subject/term remains rejected in the UI, and concurrent same-create retries converge to one active row with exact mutation-receipt idempotency. Term/year/owner checks stay enforced. Use active-only natural-identity lookup and fresh generation for explicit create after tombstone, not a label-based anti-resurrection bypass. Preserve roster for subject-only recreation and keep whole-class recreation distinct from the old deleted roster.

Read the current server creation function/unique constraints and source chain before an additive correction. Existing applied migration files are immutable. Use a new narrow migration only if current protocol needs it, retaining owner locks, signatures, search_path, ACL, receipts and all stale-delete/restore guards. Do not change n77_delete_teaching or general Sync/RLS merely to satisfy the test. No existing-user row edits/backfill and no live deletion against PO account.

Focused local/native PostgreSQL checks cover delete/create sequence, same-subject natural duplicate, multi-device old deletion receipt and stale backup failing to resurrect old IDs or suppress new IDs, owner isolation and unchanged grades in unrelated classes. Actual UI creation handlers use synthetic fixtures. Keep needed tests, but do not rerun entire historic suites or expired live A/B fixtures. Required server-binding is real readback after any certified additive migration; simulated browser checks are labeled honestly.

tasks.objective: Diagnose and fix the stationary first-account workspace preparation spinner reported on Chrome/iPhone versus rotating once in Edge. Current src/styles/app.css .first-run-status__spinner declares animation: spin .9s linear infinite but no @keyframes spin was found in tracked styles; only cloud-progress-spin exists in components.css. Verify actual styles including boot bundle before minimal correction. Keep intentional reduced-motion behavior, DOM status text and account preparation logic unchanged.
acceptance: Use a uniquely named defined keyframe in the same eagerly loaded stylesheet as the spinner so it does not depend on a later route or cached stylesheet. Normal motion must animate in Chromium and WebKit engine where available; prefers-reduced-motion must still suppress motion. No infinite forced animation that ignores user preference.

Focused synthetic render of the actual app stylesheet/status DOM at narrow/mobile size verifies a nonzero changing transform/animation, not just the presence of an animation-name declaration; reduced-motion remains static with readable status. No new account/login, SQL, restore, Product-data mutation or rerun of N71 live restore tests. This UI sub-fix does not certify/close N71's unified restore feature.
